chapter: Postwar: Chicago, Vinson, Hines and Cootie
title: Eddie Vinson, Cootie Williams and Milt Larkin
summary: Vinson contacted Gus after the Army; the talk turns to Vinson's time with Milt Larkin, Cootie, and pianist Cedric Haywood.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: And after that, then after that I got in touch -- Eddie Vinson got in touch with me. Cleanhead.
Yeah, I know. I was just thinking, he's Texas.
Yeah, he's from Houston.
Yeah, that's right. Well, where did you know him?
I knew him at the Savoy. I met him at the Savoy.
Oh.
When Jay -- he was playing with Cootie Williams' band, see.
Yeah, Cootie found him.
Yeah, I guess so.
Yeah, and he was playing with one of those territory bands when Cootie heard him, with the band you were battling.
Not Nat Towles.
Oh, I know.
Milt Larkin.
Was he with Milt Larkin's band?
He used to play in Milt Larkin's band.
Oh, I remember that he did, but that's -- Cootie took him, huh?
I guess so. I know he used to play with Milt Larkin.
Yeah, he did, but not only that, but Jacquet was in the band, that rocking band, and several good guys. You know the organ player that was with Duke? You know who I mean. 'One More Time.'
Wild Bill?
Wild Bill was in that band.
Oh, yeah.
Yeah. But it might not have been just that time. But, anyway, --
What, in Larkin's band?
Yeah, he had quite a good band. He had a guy playing -- so Wild Bill started playing guitar or something because he had a good guy on piano. Hardwick -- Cedric. Sedgewick. (Cedric Haywood -- ed)
Cedric. Sedgewick.
Yeah, Cedric. Sedgewick.
Yeah, this is him here, Cedric. Sedgewick.
Yeah.
He played with Milt Larkin.
Yeah. So that band -- and Wild Bill
Davis was playing guitar in the band. And they were both writing charts for him.
Well, he and I had been knowing each other for a long time, Cedric.
No kidding? What is he doing?
He's dead.
When did he die?
Oh, he's been dead a long time. He died, I think, before I came here to Colorado.
Oh, did he?
Yes.
Well, he never got a real break, did he, then, as a piano player?
No, not really.
Because he was a very good piano player, wasn't he?
Very good piano player. Yeah, Cedric Hollywood.
Yeah, yeah, that's right.
Yeah.
